title: Ordinary scalar extension and clopen restriction
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes and $j:Y\to X$ an open immersion. Use the small pro-etale sites, module categories, scalar-extension presentations $p$ on $X$ and $q$ on $Y$, and restriction functors of [def-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-comparison-data]. For every morphism $a:R\to S$ of sheaves of commutative rings, let $a_Y:R|_Y\to S|_Y$ be its restriction. There is a family of natural $S|_Y$-linear isomorphisms $r_S\circ E_a\cong E_{a_Y}\circ r_R$, where $r_R,r_S$ are the recorded restrictions and $E$ is the ordinary presented sheafified scalar extension. For every module sheaf $M$, every object $U$ of the opposite small pro-etale site of $Y$, and sections $s\in S|_Y(U)$ and $x\in r_RM(U)$, the forward map sends the sheafification-unit tensor $s\otimes x$ of $E_aM$ restricted to $U$ to the same tensor in $E_{a_Y}(r_RM)(U)$. No closedness, partition, flatness or boundedness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tags 03CY and 03DH, sheafification of module presheaves. Ordinary part of lem-pur-clopen-scalar-comparison-descent.

proof.text: Composition with j between the small pro-etale sites is continuous and cocontinuous. Reuse the proved generic restrictionSheafify construction and its isomorphism proof. The sheafification comparison is characterized by the equality of the local unit followed by that comparison and the restricted global unit. Cocontinuity preserves local bijectivity, and the local unit is locally bijective, so the comparison is an isomorphism.

The original changeOfRingsPresheaf commutes with this restriction by an identity sectionwise tensor isomorphism. Its naturality follows from changeOfRingsMap_tmul. Sheafify and compose with restrictionSheafify. Naturality of the sheafification unit proves the tensor formula. The sheafification adjunction and generation by pure tensors prove naturality in module morphisms.

Transport through the prescribed object equalities and map equations of p and q, then invert. Applying the inverse to the backward pure tensor formula and using hom_inv_id proves the forward tensor formula. This uses only universal properties and so applies also to zero rings and empty Y.

lean.statement:
theorem clopen_ordinary_scalar_comparison
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (p : Presentations.{t, u} X) (q : Presentations.{t, u} Y) :
    ∃ c : ∀ {R S : Sheaf (topology X) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}} (a : R ⟶ S),
        ext (p a) ⋙ res j S ≅ res j R ⋙ ext (q ((rings j).map a)),
      ∀ {R S : Sheaf (topology X) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}} (a : R ⟶ S)
        (M : Mods.{t, u} R) (U : Y.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (s : ((rings j).obj S).obj.obj U) (x : ((res j R).obj M).val.obj U),
        ((c a).hom.app M).val.app U
          (sectionTensor (p a) M
            ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale j)).op.obj U) s x) =
          sectionTensor (q ((rings j).map a)) ((res j R).obj M) U s x
